central_unknown: Whether Mercedes will introduce their ADO2 upgraded power unit this weekend, and if so, which driver (Russell or Antonelli) receives it — this determines who takes a grid penalty and becomes the top fantasy asset.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: ML projects 26.0 exp pts, ppm 1.04, LOW risk, pred Q1→P2. Mercedes historically dominant in cold conditions and at Las Vegas (Russell won here in 2024). If Antonelli receives the ADO2 power unit and takes a grid penalty, his overtaking upside makes him even more compelling. FanAmp channel also highlights Antonelli as a top pick especially if he's the experimental driver for the new engine. Championship already secured removes any team-order downside.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: ML projects 25.9 exp pts (highest projected at 40.5 pts), ppm 1.62, MEDIUM risk, pred Q5→P1. Highest projected points ceiling on the grid. Historically took fastest lap here in 2025 and led from start to finish. FanAmp ranks Verstappen among their top options. DNF risk slightly elevated at 0.11.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Lando Norris
captains.reason: ML projects 20.3 exp pts, ppm 0.92, MEDIUM risk, DNF 0.16. Rumored 10-place grid penalty creates overtaking upside. FanAmp actually ranks Norris as their top pick this week — he took pole and crossed P2 at Las Vegas last year before disqualification, and dialed in Brazil upgrades. Higher DNF risk (0.16) is a concern but ceiling is huge with penalty. Channels favor Norris but ML ranks him 5th on expected points.

buy.name: Isack Hadjar
buy.note: ML projects 12.4 exp pts, ppm 1.15, MEDIUM risk. Recently returned to F1 and was delivering 15-25 pt performances pre-injury. ReinFantasy strongly recommends Hadjar as a way to avoid the 3M trap of Perez/Bottas/Stroll. Near-100% Q3 record and consistent top-10 finisher.

buy.name: Lando Norris
buy.note: Rumored 10-place grid penalty makes him a strong overtaking play. FanAmp's top-ranked driver this weekend. ML projects Q6→P4 even without full penalty factored. Consider swapping Ferrari constructor for McLaren if running Norris.

consider.name: George Russell
consider.note: ML projects 19.3 exp pts, pred Q3→P6, MEDIUM risk. Won Las Vegas in 2024 and inherited P2 in 2025. If he takes a penalty for the ADO2 engine, he jumps significantly in value. FanAmp says if Russell takes even a 10-place penalty, he ranks above Piastri. Watch FP sessions for engine news.

consider.name: Oscar Piastri
consider.note: ML projects 17.7 exp pts, LOW risk, pred Q7→P7. Potential back-of-grid start from engine penalty (hasn't taken one all season). However, FanAmp and ReinFantasy both express skepticism — only 3 races with 30+ fantasy pts in 2026, hasn't adapted well to new regs. Hamilton only scored 26 pts from the back in Brazil. Upside capped at ~P6-P8 per channel consensus.

consider.name: Carlos Sainz
consider.note: LF1FantasyStrategy highlights Sainz's consistent form — Q3 four times, top-10 finish eight times. Good budget enabler with likely price rise potential needing only 2 pts for minimum increase.

avoid: Sergio Perez — 3M trap, serial DNFs and negative fantasy scores
Lance Stroll — finished only 2 of last 9 races, massive DNF liability
Valtteri Bottas — floor-price asset with persistent reliability issues
Fernando Alonso — Aston Martin updates haven't fixed reliability, cold conditions compound struggles

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: With only 3 races remaining, if you need to restructure away from 3M trap assets (Perez/Stroll/Bottas) toward Hadjar and better fills, this could be the last good window. ReinFantasy notes wanting 3 transfers to execute the Hadjar restructure cleanly. If you're already well-positioned, save for Abu Dhabi.

chips.name: 3x Captain
chips.reason: No sprint this weekend limits ceiling. BoxBox used 3x at Monza when Mercedes dominated with a back-of-grid Antonelli. If Mercedes ADO2 penalty situation creates a similar setup, reconsider — but current uncertainty suggests saving for a cleaner read.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Hold for post-qualifying adjustments at Abu Dhabi or if late engine penalty news breaks. Useful insurance given the ADO2 uncertainty.

chips.name: Limitless
chips.reason: BoxBox analysis showed 3x chip outscored Limitless at Monza. With only 2-3 races left, Limitless is best saved for the final round when you can go all-in without budget constraints.

watch_items: Mercedes ADO2 power unit: Which driver (Russell vs Antonelli) gets the upgraded engine? FanAmp's Terry suspects Antonelli may be the experimental driver since both championships are decided, which would flip the captain calculus.
Oscar Piastri engine penalty confirmation: Initial sims suggest back-of-grid start. Monitor official communications through FP1/FP2.
Lando Norris 10-place grid penalty: Rumored first engine component penalty since Spa. Confirm before locking lineup.

Ferrari tire warm-up issues in cold conditions: Charlotte Claire described Brazil as 'driving on ice.' Las Vegas is a November night race — if Ferrari can't get temperature into tires, avoid Ferrari constructor.

McLaren vs Ferrari constructor swap: FanAmp burned by Ferrari in Brazil (62 pts, lowest since Baku). Both channels lean McLaren constructor if Norris+Piastri are both penalized and can overtake. ML ranks Ferrari #2 (57.9 exp pts) slightly above McLaren #4 (49.0 exp pts) — a notable disagreement with narrator sentiment.

Energy deployment on the long Turn 16-to-Turn 1 straight: LF1FantasyStrategy notes cars may run out of battery charge before the end of the straight, creating yo-yo overtaking patterns that could affect fantasy points from position changes.
arc: Las Vegas is the first of the final three races, and the key strategic thread is the Mercedes ADO2 power unit introduction. If it debuts here successfully, it validates Mercedes' engine advantage in cold conditions heading into the final two rounds. The Piastri and Norris engine penalties this weekend could create a template for how grid-drop plays score under 2026 regulations — if they underperform expectations (like Hamilton's modest 26 pts from the back in Brazil), it recalibrates penalty-based captain strategies for the remaining rounds. Budget restructuring away from 3M trap assets toward Hadjar is urgent with only 2-3 races left; teams that haven't made this pivot risk bleeding points through DNFs. The Ferrari cold-weather vulnerability revealed in Brazil could persist through the season finale if conditions remain cool, making the McLaren vs Ferrari constructor decision a multi-race commitment.
